newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia confirms Tudjman won presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Croatia confirms Tudjman won presidential poll.

text.p: Croatia on Tuesday confirmed the results of its June 15 presidential election, which incumbent Franjo Tudjman won convincingly in the first round, the state news agency Hina reported.

According to the final official results released by the central electoral commission, Tudjman won 61.41 percent, Social Democrat Zdravko Tomac 21.03 percent and the joint candidate of nine opposition parties, Social Liberal Vlado Gotovac, 17.56 percent of the vote.
The turnout was put at 54.6 percent, the lowest since Croatia departed from communism to organise its first free and democratic elections in 1990, while it was still a part of the former Yugoslavia.

The 75-year old Tudjman, riding on the popularity he gained as the leader who established an independent Croatia for the first time since the 12th century, never looked threatened by the two opposition candidates.

But while the international monitors judged the election itself as "free", they said the campaign leading to it was "not fair" owing to heavy pro-Tudjman bias from state media, particularly the HRT national television network.

Tudjman, who U.S. administration officials say was treated for stomach cancer late last year, declared after the first results came out that his priority in the next five-year term would be raising Croatians' standard of living.

The ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) is considerably less popular than its charismatic leader but still holds a clear majority in parliament and does not face a new election until 1999. The HDZ also scored a landslide victory in municipal polls in April.
